scope: The arbitrary-odd-denominator finite horizon is derived in the new note. Its eventual period consumer uses the new written capacity theorem. The seven Lean lemmas cover the numerical core only.

primary_literature.authors: Kenneth G. Monks and Jonathan Yazinski
primary_literature.title: The autoconjugacy of the 3x+1 function
primary_literature.sections: Theorem 2.1 and proof Section 4.2; Theorems 2.3-2.5 for complementary-cycle context
primary_literature.inspection: Direct primary-paper inspection by root during this research pass
primary_literature.role: Credit the existing qualitative relation between rational autoconjugacy on positive integers and nondivergence. The explicit finite horizon is not claimed to be a new qualitative reduction or to have historical priority.

local_dependencies.role: Written proof of the eventual period bound K<=2q, used only after an actual cycle is proved.

comparative_input.role: Pinned specialized triadic horizon, inspected by triadic_selector. Used only to qualify that the arbitrary-odd-denominator horizon is coarser when q is a power of three; not a proof dependency of the new horizon.

open_obligations: Construct a successful candidate for every actual positive input at its own H(n,a,q).
Control nontrivial cycles or the resulting denominators; universal success in this broader class would first prove nondivergence.
verification_boundary: The complete visit count, pigeonhole, parity coding and cycle consumer are reviewed written mathematics, not fully formalized Lean claims.
